metadata.note: The Baltimore - Annapolis 'Annapolis Short Line' corridor, 1887-1950, drawn as four features split by operating company (Rule 4): Annapolis Short Line (steam, 1887-1906), Maryland Electric Railways (1906-1921), WB&A North Shore Line (1921-1935, Linthicum - Annapolis only) and Baltimore and Annapolis Railroad (1935-1950). Features 1, 2 and 4 share one geometry Camden Station - Bladen Street; feature 3 is its Linthicum - Bladen Street part. Research report: research/branches/baltimore_and_annapolis_railroad.txt.

metadata.overlap_with_other_layers: North of Linthicum the 1921-1935 WB&A era is deliberately not drawn in this layer: the WB&A cars used the WB&A main line, which belongs to the future WB&A main-line layer (queue entry washington_baltimore_and_annapolis_electric_railroad). That layer should reuse this file's WB&A colour and company string. Camden Station - Clifford is B&O track, drawn here knowingly over B&O/CSX rails (and, near Camden, the track marc.geojson's Camden Line uses).
metadata.ownership_split: Split 1906 (B&ASL -> Maryland Electric Railways Co. by consolidation, effected by 8 Aug 1906), 1921 (MER -> WB&A by purchase) and 1935 (WB&A -> Baltimore and Annapolis Railroad, 21 Aug). Not split: the 1893/94 sale and reorganization (Annapolis & Baltimore Short Line -> Baltimore & Annapolis Short Line; no evidence the operation changed), and the 1914 'new owners' (MER remained the operating company by name to 1921).
metadata.freight_only: Not drawn (Rule 1): B&A freight after 5 Feb 1950 (Annapolis to June 1968, south of Glen Burnie to 1969, Patapsco bridge lost June 1972, Glen Burnie - Annapolis abandoned 1978, stub sold to the State May 1991); the Baltimore Highlands - B&O Clifford freight interchange retained after 1921.
metadata.horsecar: None - steam from 1887, electric from 1908. Nothing trimmed (Rule 5).
metadata.excluded: Not drawn: (a) report block [5], a 1961 25-day Harundale - Camden Station commuter-rail experiment, on one uncited Wikipedia sentence; (b) report block [6], post-1950 excursion and Santa trains 'into the 1980s', undated and unrouted; (c) the Annapolis and Bay Ridge RR and the AW&B / WB&A South Shore line, which are different roads; (d) the 'Annapolis and Chesapeake Railroad' charter used as the 1921 merger vehicle.

Mileage of the line in every era - no primary figure; ~25 mi is a common round figure only.

The 20 Aug 1935 WB&A end, 21 Aug 1935 B&A start and 5 Feb 1950 last trains - secondary sources only.
The exact 1921 transfer day (late Feb PSC order vs 16 Mar 1921 Linthicum crossover).

segments.note: Annapolis and Baltimore Short Line Railroad (1887-1893/94), reorganized after the 1893 sale to George Burnham Jr. as the Baltimore and Annapolis Short Line Railroad (1894-1906); one feature, because there is no evidence the reorganization changed who ran the trains (judgment call, flagged in the report). Steam from opening (3 Mar 1887 per Wikipedia; year confirmed by the Evening Capital 26 May 1887 timetable, four trains each way daily plus Sunday trains) - no animal-power era. Trains ran Bladen Street, Annapolis - Clifford on the company's own track, then over the B&O into Camden Station. Ends 1906 because the company was consolidated into the Maryland Electric Railways Co. (effected by 8 Aug 1906), not because service stopped; the B&ASL's own schedule 'in effect May 27th, 1906' confirms it was still running trains that year. headway_min 240 is derived from four trains each way over a ~16-hour day in the 1887 timetable; later 1887-1906 frequencies are not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start year and the four-trains-daily frequency from the Evening Capital 26 May 1887 A&BSL timetable; end year from the Washington Times 8 Aug 1906 consolidation report and the Evening Capital 5 Nov 1906 B&ASL schedule eff. 27 May 1906. The 3 March 1887 day is Wikipedia only.

segments.note: Maryland Electric Railways Co., formed by consolidation of the Baltimore and Annapolis Short Line RR with the unbuilt Maryland Electric Railway Co. (effected by 8 Aug 1906, Washington Times), advertised as 'Maryland Electric Railways Co., ANNAPOLIS SHORT LINE' from autumn 1906. These years were still STEAM-hauled under the new company while electrification (begun 1906) was completed; the feature carries mode interurban because a feature has one mode (Rule 7). Electric operation completed 1908 per secondary sources (Wikipedia body, annapolisrailroadhistory.com); the day was not found. Conflict recorded: Don's Depot gives 1907 and Wikipedia/annapolisrailroadhistory.com give 1908 for the company change - superseded by the 1906 primary reports. headway_min not sourced for these steam years (left null).
sources: Segment-level: start year from the Washington Times 8 Aug 1906 (consolidation effected) and the Evening Capital 16 Nov 1906 MER 'Annapolis Short Line' ad effective 7 Nov 1906; the 1908 end of steam-only operation is secondary only (Wikipedia, annapolisrailroadhistory.com).

segments.note: Electric operation (6,600 V 25 Hz single-phase AC from 1908; changed to 1,200 V DC in 1914 under unidentified 'new owners' per Wikipedia - the Maryland Electric Railways name continues in primary sources to Feb 1921, so no split). Some steam trains continued to 1919 (Wikipedia). Electric all the way to Camden Station, half-hourly 6 a.m. - 6 p.m. then hourly-ish to 11.35 p.m., 45 minutes end to end, per the Evening Capital 14 Jun 1910 ad - headway_min 30 is that ad's daytime figure for 1910 and is not sourced for other years. From 1914 the route north of Clifford used the B&O's new Clifford Jct - Westport - Carroll Jct connection (Wikipedia). Ends 1921: sale to the WB&A approved by MER shareholders early Feb 1921, by WB&A stockholders 18 Feb 1921, PSC hearing 21 Feb 1921 with order 'within a few days'; WB&A operation began Feb-Mar 1921 (day not fixed).
sources: Segment-level: electric half-hourly service into Camden from the Evening Capital 14 Jun 1910 ad; MER still named operator in the Evening Capital 25 Oct 1912; end year from the Washington Times 19 Feb 1921 and Evening Capital 22 Feb 1921. The 1908 electric start and the 1914 AC-to-DC change are secondary only (Wikipedia, trains-and-railroads.com).

segments.note: The WB&A bought the Short Line in 1921 and ran it as its 'North Shore' line. DRAWN ONLY LINTHICUM - ANNAPOLIS: north of Linthicum the cars ran over the WB&A main line via the Linthicum crossover (opened 16 Mar 1921) to the WB&A terminal at Howard and Lombard Streets, and that stretch belongs to the separate WB&A main-line layer (not yet built), so it is not drawn twice. Most of the old Short Line track Linthicum - Westport was abandoned after the purchase. WB&A in receivership from Jan 1931; trains ran until the WB&A ceased operation on 20 Aug 1935. headway_min 30 is an ESTIMATE carried over from the 1910 MER half-hourly ad; no WB&A-era timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: start year from primary newspapers (Washington Herald 4 Feb 1921; Evening Capital 3 Feb 1921 on routing over the WB&A; Washington Times 19 Feb 1921; Evening Capital 22 Feb 1921). The 20 Aug 1935 end is secondary only (Wikipedia). Headway not sourced.

UNESTABLISHED ALIGNMENT: Linthicum - Westport, about 4.9 mi. Which track carried B&A cars here 1935-1950 is not established (report block [4]): the old Short Line track Linthicum - Westport was reported abandoned in 1921 apart from the Baltimore Highlands - Clifford freight interchange, and the WB&A main line north of Pumphrey was sold to the State Roads Commission only in 1941. Drawn as the most plausible route: the Short Line grade Linthicum - Baltimore Highlands - Clifford (the alignment the Light RailLink reuses and OSM tags 'Maryland Electric', and on which B&A freight later reached the Patapsco crossing), then B&O track via Westport to Carroll and Camden, matching Wikipedia's 'through Westport to Carroll Junction and the Camden Cutoff'. The alternative - the ex-WB&A main line via Pumphrey, which the B&A's 1951 bus station list follows - is mapped in neither OSM nor OHM north of Linthicum (OHM's WB&A way -200442176 ends at Linthicum), so it could not be drawn. Treat this leg as a plausible placement, not a sourced one.

segments.note: The Baltimore and Annapolis Railroad Co., formed by the Short Line bondholders, bought back the North Shore property at the 1935 WB&A sale and took over on 21 Aug 1935 'for continuous operation', running electric cars into Camden Station by agreement with the B&O. Ridership 990,000 in 1939 and 2,000,000 in 1943; company buses ran alongside the trains from 1938. PSC approved discontinuance Dec 1949; last rail passenger service 5 Feb 1950, buses thereafter. Freight continued (Annapolis to 1968, south of Glen Burnie to 1969, a Glen Burnie stub into the 1980s) - context only, not drawn (Rule 1). The Linthicum - Westport track used in this era is NOT ESTABLISHED; see geometry_quality. Conflict recorded: Wikipedia's WB&A article lead says successors carried passengers 'until the late 1950s'; every specific source gives 5 Feb 1950, adopted here. headway_min 60 is an ESTIMATE; no timetable for this era was read.
sources: Segment-level: SECONDARY SOURCES ONLY - the 21 Aug 1935 takeover and the 5 Feb 1950 last trains are from Wikipedia's Baltimore and Annapolis Railroad and Camden Station articles and annapolisrailroadhistory.com (Camden 1935-1950; Bladen St and Earleigh Heights 'Closed: 1950'); no primary newspaper was found for either date. The Feb 1952 Official Guide's B&A table is bus-only and is not evidence either way.
